s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pruritic skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure
salient_findings: Numerous small blisters on ears and vermillion border
Erythematous papules and crusts on cheeks, neck, and lower arms
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with skin eruption
Eruption appeared 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
Patient had episode of malaise and headache 2 weeks before presentation
No history of photosensitivity
No use of topical or systemic photosensitizers
Serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies were detectable
PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen
Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable
Laboratory tests, including differential blood count and serum porphyrins, were unremarkable

shortlist.label: Parvovirus B19-associated erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Detectable serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen

shortlist.label: Polymorphic light eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Acute pruritic skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Skin eruption with helical thickening, erythema, and numerous small blisters

shortlist.label: Hydroa vacciniforme
shortlist.why_kept: Skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure

shortlist.label: Pityriasis lichenoides et varioliformis acuta
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic skin eruption with papules and vesicles

raw.rationale: The presence of serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA in the lesional skin biopsy specimen, along with the patient's symptoms and lack of other explanatory factors, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Polymorphic light eruption
rejected.why: While the eruption appeared after sun exposure, standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable, and the presence of PVB19 DNA points towards a viral etiology rather than a pure photosensitive reaction.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and the specific findings of helical thickening, erythema, and small vesicles, especially with the detection of PVB19 DNA, are more suggestive of a parvovirus B19-associated condition than erythema multiforme, which often has a more targetoid appearance and can be associated with a broader range of triggers including infections and medications.

rejected.label: Hydroa vacciniforme
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more severe photosensitivity and characteristic vacciniform scars, which were not mentioned in the case description. The presence of PVB19 DNA and the clinical presentation do not align well with hydroa vacciniforme.

rejected.label: Pityriasis lichenoides et varioliformis acuta
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and the laboratory findings, particularly the detection of PVB19 DNA in the lesional skin, do not support this diagnosis, which typically involves more papular and necrotic lesions without a clear association with parvovirus B19 infection.
